release_context.label: Latest monthly labor-market releases available as of October 2, 2026
release_context.note: Values are public, seasonally adjusted headline indicators from BLS series as displayed by FRED. Data may be revised.

indicators.label: Unemployment rate
indicators.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED
indicators.interpretation: Headline unemployment rose to 4.2, a weaker signal for worker security.

indicators.label: Labor force participation
indicators.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED
indicators.interpretation: Participation rose to 61.8, improving worker availability.

indicators.label: Total nonfarm payrolls
indicators.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED
indicators.interpretation: Payroll employment increased by 29 thousand to 159,044, a positive hiring signal.

indicators.label: Job openings
indicators.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED
indicators.interpretation: Openings fell by 256 thousand to 7,079, pointing to softer unmet labor demand.

indicators.label: U-6 labor underutilization
indicators.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED
indicators.interpretation: Broader labor underutilization eased to 7.6, but still captures marginal attachment and involuntary part-time work.

indicators.label: Production and nonsupervisory hourly earnings
indicators.source_name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED
indicators.interpretation: Hourly pay for production and nonsupervisory workers rose to $32.60, a worker-pay gauge to read alongside inflation and hours.

sources.name: BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey
